title: Bar chart
summary: A bar chart: values by category as columns or bars, grouped or stacked (also as shares), with a value axis from zero, a legend that hides series, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor, a summary in words and the same data as a table; with bin, a histogram of one measure.

template.description: Template variant name for SfBaseElement external templates.

root-class.description: Classes added to the root element the component draws.

root-style.description: Inline style declarations set on the root element the component draws, custom properties included.

label.description: What the chart shows, in a few words: its accessible name, the table's caption and the file name of an export. Required in practice: without it the chart is named «Диаграмма».

palette.description: The seriess' colours as a named set, by place, each a light and a dark tone that change with the theme and hold 3:1 against surfaces 0-2: theme (the theme's own tones, as before), vivid (8, the first the brand's), soft (8, muted), warm (6), cool (6), brand (4 steps of the primary family, for ordered data). Past its size a set starts again. colors wins for the seriess it names.

x.description: The field of the categories; the first field when unset. With bin, the measure cut into intervals; the first numeric field when unset.

y.description: The field of the values, or a comma list of fields, one series per field (the wide form); every numeric field when unset. With bin, a weight summed per interval (an amount), or a count of the rows when unset.

series.description: The long form: one series per distinct value of this field, the values from the first y field.

bin.description: A histogram: none draws the rows as given; auto cuts the x measure into intervals of one round width (about Sturges' count for the rows) and draws one bar per interval, the count of its rows; a number is the intervals' width. y, when given, is a weight summed per interval instead of a count. The bars touch and the axis is marked at the intervals' edges; sort does not apply.

x-scale.description: auto reads the categories: dates stand in time order and read as dates, anything else stays in the order given. A bar chart's axis is always bands.

y-max.description: The end of the value axis; the data's own when unset. Ignored by normalized.

stack.description: none: the series' bars stand side by side in each category; stacked: on one another, positive up and negative down from zero; normalized: each stack as shares of its whole, 0–100 %.

lines.description: A comma list of series drawn as lines with points over the bars, not as bars: a plan over the facts, a margin over the revenue. Only on vertical bars; a horizontal chart draws every series as bars.

line-axis.description: shared: the lines on the bars' value axis; own: the lines on a scale of their own, its ticks on the far side, for values of another kind (a share over a sum). A normalized stack always gives the lines their own scale.

line-format.description: The format of the lines' values on their own scale, in the tooltip, the live line and the table, as y-format; y-format when unset.

orientation.description: vertical: columns over categories along the bottom; horizontal: bars from the left, categories down the side, for long names and rankings.

sort.description: The order of the categories: as given, or by their total, smallest or largest first.

value-labels.description: end: each bar's value (a stack's total) at its end, where it fits; never in normalized.

legend.description: auto shows the legend above the plot when there are two series or more. Each entry is a button that hides and shows its series.

tooltip.description: axis: under the pointer or the cursor, every series' value in that category; in normalized, its share and its value.

grid.description: value: guide lines across the plot at the value ticks; none: only the zero line.

x-label.description: The name of the categories, under a vertical chart; it heads the table's first column (the x field's own name when unset).

y-label.description: The name of the values, above a vertical chart and under a horizontal one.

x-format.description: For dates as categories: auto, or an Intl date style (short, medium, long, full). With bin, the measure's number format for the intervals' edges (number when auto).

y-format.description: number, integer, decimal-<n>, percent (a share 0..1), compact or currency-<CODE>, in the page's language.

size.description: The rung of the size ladder: the plot's height, the text and the gaps. 1/2 for a card, 2 for a page of its own.

table.description: The same data as a table: toggle offers a button that swaps the plot for it, visible shows it under the plot, hidden keeps it for screen readers only. Never none: the table is the chart's text.

summary.description: auto: a sentence of the data (how many categories, each series' highest and lowest), said before the plot and kept for screen readers. The description slot adds the host's own words.

data-state.description: auto: ready with data, empty without. loading draws the frame without bars; error offers «Повторить», which sends refresh.

items.description: The data: a list of records ([{city, sales}, …]) or an object of columns. One bar per category and series. A missing value (null, '', a word) is a gap: no bar, never a zero.

names.description: What each series is called, by its key: {sales: «Продажи»}. A series without a name is called by its key.

colors.description: What colour each series is, by its key, bars and lines alike: {fact: 'primary', plan: 'neutral'}. A colour is a Framework role (primary, secondary, tertiary, neutral, success, warning, error, info), which follows the theme, or any CSS colour or variable; anything else is dropped with a console report, as is a colour under 3:1 against the background (drawn all the same). A series without one keeps the palette by its place. In forced colours a series is its dash.

hidden-series.description: The keys of the series the person hid with the legend.

reset.summary: Shows every series again and takes the cursor away.

sf-chart-bar-toggle.summary: The person hid or showed a series with its legend button; applied at once (the vocabulary's local toggle).

sf-chart-bar-select.summary: The person chose a bar: a click on the plot, or Enter or Space on the keyboard cursor.

sf-chart-bar-refresh.summary: The person asked for the data again from the error state; the host loads it and sets items.

accessibility.focus: One Tab stop on the plot, then the legend buttons and the table button. The summary is the plot's description; each cursor move is said politely.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-chart-bar to compare values across categories, or the parts of each category's whole (stack).
do_not: Do not draw a chart without a label
Do not replace missing values with zero
Do not use it for a long series over time; that is sf-chart-line
